subject: Renewal: proposal for staged annualization + exit band (Nimbus Dataworks)
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@nimbusdataworks.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: Finance <finance@nimbusdataworks.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal restructure request — staged annualization + exit band

Stephanie —

Thanks for the continuous support this year. We're kicking off our renewal conversation for NW-4821 and want to propose a structure that helps us smooth spend while we scale our product usage. High level ask: convert to a 3-year commitment with an accelerated ramp and a defined early-exit band so we can avoid surprise budget impacts in Y1.

Proposed sketch (from our side):
- Year 1: 50% of target committed capacity (ability to burst to 80%)
- Year 2: 100% committed
- Year 3: 150% committed
- Auto-renew for subsequent 12 months unless we give 60 days notice; but we need an exit band that allows a 20% reduction (with a defined prorate) in any renewal year in the first 24 months.

We can be flexible on credits vs. upfront if there are incentives to annualize earlier. Can Redwood share a proposal that includes: convertible credits, co-terming with our financial year (we prefer co-term to 2028-01-01), and an operational SLA credit if latency targets slip >10%?

Attached is a one-page from our procurement team with preferred commercial guardrails (nimbus-requested-terms-v1.pdf). Happy to jump on a call this week.

—Oliver
VP of Platform, Nimbus Dataworks
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@nimbusdataworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal restructure request — staged annualization + exit band

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear sketch and the attachment. We can absolutely support a staged annualization approach and provide options that balance your runway with predictable economics. Looping in Marissa (AM), Karthik (pricing/structures), and Grace (CS/SLAs) to scope a concrete Mutual Action Plan.

Quick replies to your asks: 
- Convertible credits: yes — we can convert a portion of any remaining credits into committed capacity with a frontloaded discount in Y1.
- Co-term to 2028-01-01: workable; we'll surface pro-rated figures and a co-term amendment.
- Exit band / prorate: we can offer an early-exit band with a tapering prorate (e.g., 20% reduction allowed in years 1–2 with a defined 30-day notice and a standard unwind fee).
- SLA credit request: we'll propose an SLA credit table and a measurable latency metric threshold. Grace, can you propose language we can agree to operationally?

Marissa / Karthik — can you prepare a 1-sheet with two commercial structures: (A) 3-year staircase (50/100/150) with convertible credits and (B) 2-year hybrid (75/125) that gives Nimbus more flexibility but slightly higher unit price. If possible, include the math on unit cost per token for each year and the impact of early-exit band on NPV.

Oliver — can we target Friday 10/08 for a 30-min alignment call? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short MAP doc to capture milestones.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbus — draft commercial options (internal)

Team —

I put together a quick draft spreadsheet (redwood-proposed-symphony-structure.xlsx) with two structures as requested. Key points / tradeoffs: 

Option A — Symphony Staircase (3yr)
- Year 1 commit: 50% baseline (burst to 80% allowed)
- Year 2 commit: 100% baseline
- Year 3 commit: 150% baseline
- Convertible credits: up to 25% of unused hosted credits to be applied to Year 1 commit (frontloaded discount 12%)
- Early-exit band: 20% reduction allowed in Y1/Y2 with a 30% unwind fee on the reduced portion in the first 12 months, taper to 10% unwind in months 13–24.
- Co-term: adjust to 2028-01-01 with prorated invoice for partial first/last periods.
- SLA: propose 5% service credit per calendar month when latency p95 > baseline +10% (cumulative cap 15% annually).

Option B — Hybrid Flex (2yr)
- Year 1 commit: 75% baseline
- Year 2 commit: 125% baseline
- Higher unit price (approx +8%) but lower unwind fee and immediate narrower exit band (10%).

Action items for next steps: 
- Karthik: provide final NPV numbers and token-unit comparisons for both options. Include an example showing how convertible credits flow into Year 1.
- Grace: confirm whether SLA language as written is operationally measurable and whether we need a Service Review cadence (quarterly).
- Stephanie: will draft a short MAP to present to Nimbus and include milestone dates (signature target, billing cutover, onboarding timeline).

I also drafted sample contract language to cover co-terming and the unwind fee — keeping procurement-friendly phrasing.

Marissa
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@nimbusdataworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Finance <finance@nimbusdataworks.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal restructure request — staged annualization + exit band

Oliver —

Thanks again for the outline. Attached is our initial proposal bundle (redwood-proposed-symphony-structure.xlsx) and a short MAP that lays out milestones and decision points. Key proposal highlights: 

- We recommend Option A (Symphony Staircase) as it minimizes near-term cash exposure for Nimbus while preserving volume-based unit economics as usage ramps.
- Convertible credits: we propose converting up to 20% of remaining hosted credits into Year 1 committed capacity with a 10% frontload discount.
- Early-exit band: 20% allowed in Y1–Y2 with a stepped unwind fee (30% -> 10%).
- Co-term: target date 2028-01-01; we will pro-rate first/last period invoices.
- SLA: Grace suggests the p95 latency threshold and a quarterly Service Review. Draft SLA table is in the attachment.

Next steps (proposed MAP):
1) Internal sign-off on commercial option (Nimbus) — target 10/08
2) Sign MAP and issue PO — target 10/15
3) Sign contract amendment (DocuSign link included) and schedule onboarding ramp kickoff — target 10/22

DocuSign link: see attachment DocuSign-NW-4821-link.txt (live link will be created once legal and finance align).

Oliver, would you like Marissa to join the 10/08 call to walk through the line items and NPV? If yes, reply with preferred time and we'll lock in the invite.

Best,
Stephanie
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
